coverage: All 42 sections of the novel: every named character, household member, local figure, pet and off-stage acquaintance, plus named authors, artists and literary characters, with spoiler-gated reminders for deaths, marriages and changes reported in "Time Passes" and "The Lighthouse".

entities.name: Mrs. Ramsay
entities.subtitle: Mr. Ramsay's wife; mother of eight
entities.body: Wife of the philosopher Mr. Ramsay and mother of their eight children. She is hosting her family and a houseful of guests at their summer house on the Isle of Skye, and is knitting a stocking for the lighthouse keeper's little boy.

snapshots.body: A bracketed passage in "Time Passes" reports that she died suddenly one night. The next morning Mr. Ramsay, stumbling along a dark passage, stretched out his arms for her, and they stayed empty.

entities.name: Mr. Ramsay
entities.subtitle: Mrs. Ramsay's husband; a philosopher
entities.body: Mrs. Ramsay's husband and father of their eight children, a philosopher who lectures at universities. Blunt to the point of cruelty about facts, he tells James the weather will be too bad to go to the Lighthouse.

snapshots.body: Now a widower. A bracketed passage reports that his wife died suddenly one night; the next morning he stretched out his arms for her in a dark passage, and they stayed empty.
Years after that summer he is back at the house, now a widower, determined to sail to the Lighthouse with Cam and James, and has already lost his temper over the delays.
At seventy-one he has sailed with Cam and James to the Lighthouse. He praised James's steering at last, and sprang onto the rock with his parcel for the keepers like a young man.

entities.name: Lily Briscoe
entities.subtitle: A painter; guest of the Ramsays
entities.body: An unmarried painter in her thirties who keeps house for her father in London and is staying in the village near the Ramsays for the summer. She is painting a picture on the lawn with Mrs. Ramsay and James in the window as her subject.

snapshots.body: Years after that summer, she has come back to the Ramsays' house, arriving late one September evening on the same train as Mr. Carmichael.

Back at the house after ten years, now forty-four, she has set up her easel on the same spot to finish the picture she never completed. Mr. Ramsay's demands and her anger at Mrs. Ramsay's death make it hard to begin.
Sensing that Mr. Ramsay has reached the Lighthouse, she draws a last line down the center of her canvas and finishes her picture: "I have had my vision."

entities.name: James Ramsay
entities.subtitle: The Ramsays' youngest son
entities.body: The Ramsays' youngest son, six years old, who longs to go to the Lighthouse. He sits at his mother's feet cutting pictures out of a store catalogue.

snapshots.body: Now sixteen, ten years after that first summer. Sullen and resentful, he has agreed under pressure to sail to the Lighthouse with his father and Cam.
Steering the boat to the Lighthouse, he has finally been praised by his father ("Well done!") and is quietly delighted, though he won't show it.

entities.name: Cam Ramsay
entities.subtitle: The Ramsays' youngest daughter
entities.body: Mr. and Mrs. Ramsay's youngest daughter, a small, wild and fiercely independent child.

snapshots.body: About seventeen now, ten years after that first summer. She has reluctantly agreed to sail to the Lighthouse with her father and James.

entities.name: Prue Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' daughters
entities.body: One of the older Ramsay daughters, gentle with the younger children; her mother is sure she will grow into a great beauty.

snapshots.body: A bracketed passage in "Time Passes" reports that she was married in May, given away on her father's arm.
A bracketed passage reports that she died the same summer as her wedding, of some illness connected with childbirth.

entities.name: Andrew Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' sons
entities.body: One of the older Ramsay sons, clever and gifted at mathematics, who likes hunting for crabs on the shore.

snapshots.body: A bracketed passage in "Time Passes" reports that he was killed in France during the war, among twenty or thirty young men blown up by a shell; his death was instantaneous.

entities.name: Nancy Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' daughters
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' daughters, a solitary, brooding girl who likes to escape to her attic or her own rock pools.

entities.name: Jasper Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' sons
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' sons, a nonchalant boy who likes to go out shooting birds.

entities.name: Roger Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' sons
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' sons; with his sister Nancy he spends whole days scampering wild about the countryside.

entities.name: Rose Ramsay
entities.subtitle: One of the Ramsays' daughters
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' daughters, clever with her hands: she makes costumes, arranges flowers and tables, and collects shells and stones.

entities.name: The Ramsays
entities.subtitle: Mr. and Mrs. Ramsay and their eight children
entities.body: The philosopher Mr. Ramsay, his wife and their eight children: Prue, Andrew, Nancy, Jasper, Roger, Rose, Cam and James. They spend summers in a shabby rented house on the Isle of Skye, always full of guests.

snapshots.body: The family has lost Mrs. Ramsay, who died suddenly one night, as a bracketed passage reports.
In the years after Mrs. Ramsay's sudden death, Prue has died after childbirth and Andrew has been killed in the war. The summer house stands empty.

entities.name: William Bankes
entities.subtitle: A botanist; Mr. Ramsay's old friend
entities.body: An old friend of Mr. Ramsay's, a widowed botanist in his sixties, scrupulous and very clean. He is lodging in the village in the same house as Lily Briscoe.

snapshots.body: Ten years on, Mr. Ramsay recalls that there was once talk of Lily marrying William Bankes, but nothing came of it.

Lily remembers their long friendship, one of the pleasures of her life: summer outings to Hampton Court where he talked about perspective and architecture. She loved William Bankes, though they never married.

entities.name: Charles Tansley
entities.subtitle: A young academic; Mr. Ramsay's admirer
entities.body: A poor, awkward young scholar from a working family, one of Mr. Ramsay's admirers, invited to stay for the holiday. The Ramsay children mock him as "the little atheist".

snapshots.body: Ten years on, Lily reflects that he has got his fellowship, married, and lives at Golders Green. During the war she heard him preaching brotherly love from a platform.

entities.name: Augustus Carmichael
entities.subtitle: An elderly poet; guest of the Ramsays
entities.body: An elderly guest who spends his days drowsing on the Ramsays' lawn. He writes poetry, keeps to himself, and seems to want nothing from anyone.

snapshots.body: A bracketed passage in "Time Passes" reports that he published a volume of poems that had an unexpected success; people said the war had revived interest in poetry.
He has become famous for his poetry, and old work of his is being published. Lily has heard that when Andrew Ramsay was killed he "lost all interest in life".

entities.name: Minta Doyle
entities.subtitle: A young guest of the Ramsays
entities.body: A young woman of twenty-four staying with the Ramsays for the summer, a lively, harum-scarum tomboy.

snapshots.body: On a cliff walk, Paul Rayley has asked her to marry him, and she has evidently said yes. She has lost her grandmother's brooch on the beach.
Ten years on, she has married Paul Rayley and they have two little boys. Lily imagines the marriage turning out badly after the first year or so, with bitter late-night scenes.
Lily's picture of the Rayleys' marriage: after a dangerous stage it has settled into a friendship, even though Paul has taken up with another woman.

entities.name: Paul Rayley
entities.subtitle: A young guest of the Ramsays
entities.body: A good-looking, kindly young man staying with the Ramsays for the summer, not especially clever. Mrs. Ramsay is fond of him.

snapshots.body: On a cliff walk he has asked Minta Doyle to marry him, and feels he owes his courage to Mrs. Ramsay.
Ten years on, he is married to Minta and they have two little boys. Lily imagines the marriage turning out badly after the first year or so, with jealous, bitter scenes.
Lily's picture of the Rayleys: he plays chess in coffeehouses and has taken up with another woman who shares his political views, which has oddly steadied the marriage.

entities.name: The Rayleys
entities.subtitle: Paul Rayley and Minta Doyle as a couple
entities.body: Mrs. Ramsay's name for Paul Rayley and Minta Doyle as a couple, now that the two young guests are engaged.

snapshots.body: Paul and Minta, married for years now, with two little boys. Lily imagines the marriage turning out badly after the first year or so.

entities.name: Mrs. Beckwith
entities.subtitle: An elderly guest at the house
entities.body: A kind old lady staying at the Ramsays' house, who likes to sketch.

entities.name: Mrs. McNab
entities.subtitle: An old local woman who looks after the house
entities.body: An old local woman, nearly seventy, who comes in to clean and look after the Ramsays' summer house.

snapshots.body: Summoned in a hurry by a letter from one of the young ladies of the family, she and Mrs. Bast have worked to rescue the decaying house before the family's return.

entities.name: Mrs. Bast
entities.subtitle: A local woman helping Mrs. McNab
entities.body: An elderly local woman who helps Mrs. McNab clean and restore the house. She never knew the Ramsays, having lived in Glasgow at the time.

entities.name: George Bast
entities.subtitle: Mrs. Bast's son
entities.body: Mrs. Bast's son, who catches the rats and cuts the grass while the house is put in order.

entities.name: Macalister
entities.subtitle: An old local boatman
entities.body: An old local fisherman with earrings, who sails the Ramsays across the bay to the Lighthouse.

entities.name: Macalister’s boy
entities.subtitle: Young crew member on Macalister's boat
entities.body: The boy who crews for old Macalister, rowing and fishing on the trip to the Lighthouse.

entities.name: Mildred
entities.subtitle: A servant in the Ramsay household
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' servants: she does the cooking, and also helps put the youngest children to bed.

entities.name: Marie, the Swiss girl
entities.subtitle: A Swiss maid in the Ramsay household
entities.body: A young Swiss maid working for the Ramsays. Her father is dying of cancer at home in the mountains of the Grisons.

entities.name: Ellen
entities.subtitle: A maid in the Ramsay household
entities.body: One of the Ramsays' maids, who clears away tea and serves at dinner.

entities.name: Marthe
entities.subtitle: A maid in the Ramsay household
entities.body: A maid who serves the Bœuf en Daube at dinner, taking the cover off the dish with a flourish.

entities.name: Kennedy
entities.subtitle: The Ramsays' gardener
entities.body: The Ramsays' gardener, so handsome that Mrs. Ramsay can't bring herself to dismiss him, though he is incurably lazy.

snapshots.body: Mrs. Bast says old Kennedy was supposed to look after the garden, but his leg went bad after he fell from a cart, and it was neglected for a year or so.

entities.name: Davie Macdonald
entities.subtitle: A later gardener
entities.body: Someone who took over the Ramsays' garden in the years after Kennedy hurt his leg, according to Mrs. Bast.

entities.name: Sorley
entities.subtitle: The lighthouse keeper
entities.body: The keeper of the Lighthouse. Mrs. Ramsay is knitting stockings for his little boy, who has a tuberculous hip.

entities.name: Badger
entities.subtitle: An old dog
entities.body: Old Badger, apparently the family dog, so old he has no teeth left; the children say even he bit Charles Tansley.

entities.name: Frisk
entities.subtitle: Mr. Ramsay's childhood dog
entities.body: A dog Mr. Ramsay had when he was a little boy.

entities.name: Joseph and Mary
entities.subtitle: Mrs. Ramsay's names for two rooks
entities.body: Mrs. Ramsay's names for a pair of rooks that roost in the trees outside. Joseph is the difficult old father rook with half his wing feathers missing.

entities.name: Elsie
entities.subtitle: Someone in a house in the town
entities.body: Someone Mrs. Ramsay says goodbye to as she leaves the little house in the town where she has visited a woman. The text does not say who Elsie is.

entities.name: Edward
entities.subtitle: Sender of the boar's skull
entities.body: Someone who sent the Ramsay children the boar's skull nailed up in their nursery. The text does not say who he is.

entities.name: Aunt Camilla
entities.subtitle: Mrs. Ramsay's aunt
entities.body: Mrs. Ramsay's aunt, whom she calls the most beautiful woman she ever saw, and a worse exaggerator than herself.

entities.name: Uncle James
entities.subtitle: A relative of the family
entities.body: An uncle who brought Mrs. Ramsay an opal necklace from India. The text does not say whose uncle he is.

entities.name: Mr. Langley
entities.subtitle: An acquaintance of the Ramsays
entities.body: An acquaintance who had been round the world dozens of times but was never so seasick as when Mr. Ramsay took him to the Lighthouse.

entities.name: Miss Giddings
entities.subtitle: An acquaintance of the Ramsays
entities.body: A woman who almost jumped out of her skin when Mr. Ramsay shouted a line of poetry at her.

entities.name: Mr. Paunceforte
entities.subtitle: A painter who visited the area
entities.body: A painter whose visit three years earlier set a fashion among local artists for pale green-and-gray pictures with lemon-colored boats and pink women on the beach.

entities.name: Mrs. Doyle
entities.subtitle: Minta Doyle's mother
entities.body: Minta Doyle's mother, whom Mrs. Ramsay privately calls "the Owl". She keeps a parrot that dominates the conversation at home.

entities.name: The Owl and the Poker
entities.subtitle: Minta Doyle's parents
entities.body: Mrs. Ramsay's private nicknames for Minta Doyle's parents, a rather portentous couple ("He wore a wig in the House of Commons and she ably assisted him at the head of the stairs"). Mrs. Ramsay feels responsible to them for Minta's conduct.

entities.name: The Mannings
entities.subtitle: Old acquaintances of Mrs. Ramsay
entities.body: A family both Mrs. Ramsay and William Bankes know. She last visited them twenty years ago at their house on the Thames at Marlow.

entities.name: Carrie Manning
entities.subtitle: An old acquaintance of Mrs. Ramsay
entities.body: One of the Mannings of Marlow, whom Mrs. Ramsay last saw twenty years ago. Mr. Bankes has just had a letter from her.

entities.name: Herbert
entities.subtitle: Remembered from a day at Marlow
entities.body: Someone Mrs. Ramsay remembers killing a wasp with a teaspoon on the riverbank during a visit to the Mannings twenty years ago; apparently one of their household.

entities.name: George Manning
entities.subtitle: A famous admirer of Mrs. Ramsay
entities.body: A famous man who, like Mr. Wallace, used to come and talk alone with Mrs. Ramsay by her fire in the evening.

entities.name: Mr. Wallace
entities.subtitle: A famous admirer of Mrs. Ramsay
entities.body: A famous man who, like George Manning, used to come and talk alone with Mrs. Ramsay by her fire in the evening.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.subtitle: English playwright and poet
entities.body: The English playwright and poet (1564–1616), for Mr. Ramsay the obvious yardstick of lasting literary fame.

entities.name: Sir Walter Scott
entities.subtitle: Scottish novelist and poet
entities.body: Scottish novelist and poet (1771–1832), author of the Waverley novels, a series of historical novels named after the first of them, Waverley (1814).

entities.name: Steenie Mucklebackit
entities.subtitle: Character in Scott’s The Antiquary
entities.body: A young fisherman in Sir Walter Scott's novel The Antiquary (1816), whose drowning and funeral are among the book's best-known scenes.

entities.name: The Mucklebackits
entities.subtitle: Family in Scott’s The Antiquary
entities.body: A family of poor fisherfolk in Sir Walter Scott's novel The Antiquary (1816). The "poor old crazed creature" in their cottage is the aged grandmother, Elspeth.

entities.name: Leo Tolstoy
entities.subtitle: Russian novelist
entities.body: Russian novelist (1828–1910), author of War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

entities.name: Count Vronsky
entities.subtitle: Character in Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina
entities.body: The dashing cavalry officer with whom Anna has her fateful love affair in Tolstoy's novel Anna Karenina (1878).

entities.name: George Eliot
entities.subtitle: English novelist
entities.body: Pen name of Mary Ann Evans (1819–1880), English novelist whose Middlemarch was first published in several volumes.

entities.name: Jane Austen
entities.subtitle: English novelist
entities.body: English novelist (1775–1817), author of Pride and Prejudice and Emma.

entities.name: Honoré de Balzac
entities.subtitle: French novelist
entities.body: French novelist (1799–1850), whose many novels of French society make up The Human Comedy.

entities.name: David Hume
entities.subtitle: Scottish philosopher
entities.body: Scottish philosopher and historian (1711–1776), one of the great figures of British empiricist philosophy.

entities.name: John Locke
entities.subtitle: English philosopher
entities.body: English philosopher (1632–1704), author of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding.

entities.name: George Berkeley
entities.subtitle: Irish philosopher
entities.body: Irish philosopher and bishop (1685–1753), who argued that material things exist only by being perceived.

entities.name: Thomas Carlyle
entities.subtitle: Scottish historian and essayist
entities.body: Scottish historian and essayist (1795–1881), a hugely influential moral teacher to the Victorians.

entities.name: Virgil
entities.subtitle: Roman poet
entities.body: Roman poet (70–19 BC), author of the Aeneid.

entities.name: Henrik Ibsen
entities.subtitle: Norwegian playwright
entities.body: Norwegian playwright (1828–1906), author of A Doll's House. "To go to Ibsen" means to see one of his plays.

entities.name: Voltaire
entities.subtitle: French writer
entities.body: French writer and philosopher of the Enlightenment (1694–1778).

entities.name: Madame de Staël
entities.subtitle: French writer
entities.body: French writer and intellectual (1766–1817), famous for her salon and her opposition to Napoleon.

entities.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
entities.subtitle: French emperor
entities.body: French general and emperor (1769–1821).

entities.name: Lord Rosebery
entities.subtitle: British prime minister
entities.body: British Liberal statesman (1847–1929), prime minister in 1894–95.

entities.name: Thomas Creevey
entities.subtitle: English politician and diarist
entities.body: English politician (1768–1838) whose gossipy letters and diaries, published in 1903 as The Creevey Papers, describe Regency politics and society.

entities.name: Michelangelo
entities.subtitle: Italian Renaissance artist
entities.body: Italian Renaissance sculptor, painter and architect (1475–1564), painter of the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

entities.name: Raphael
entities.subtitle: Italian Renaissance painter
entities.body: Italian Renaissance painter (1483–1520), celebrated for his paintings of the Madonna and Child.

entities.name: Titian
entities.subtitle: Venetian painter
entities.body: Venetian Renaissance painter (c. 1488–1576). "Titians" means painters of his greatness.

entities.name: Charles Darwin
entities.subtitle: English naturalist
entities.body: English naturalist (1809–1882), who set out the theory of evolution by natural selection. "Darwins" means scientists of his greatness.

entities.name: Rembrandt
entities.subtitle: Dutch painter
entities.body: Dutch painter (1606–1669); Mr. Bankes has seen his paintings in Amsterdam.

entities.name: Giotto
entities.subtitle: Italian painter
entities.body: Italian painter (c. 1267–1337) whose frescoes in Padua's Arena Chapel are among his best-known works.

entities.name: Queen Victoria
entities.subtitle: British queen
entities.body: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901. The blue ribbon she wears in the picture is the sash of the Order of the Garter.

entities.name: The Brothers Grimm
entities.subtitle: German collectors of fairy tales
entities.body: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, German scholars who collected folk and fairy tales, including "The Fisherman and His Wife", which Mrs. Ramsay reads to James.

entities.name: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
entities.subtitle: Victorian poet
entities.body: Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1809–1892), Poet Laureate, whose poem “The Charge of the Light Brigade” (1854) supplies the lines Mr. Ramsay keeps reciting.

entities.name: William Cowper
entities.subtitle: English poet
entities.body: William Cowper (1731–1800), whose poem “The Castaway” describes a sailor washed overboard and drowned alone; Mr. Ramsay quotes its lines.
